content: Hello—have a capital gain you want to defer?
Yes. I just sold stock with a large gain. Can a QOF help me?

Yes—invest the **gain amount** into a **Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF)** within **180 days** to **defer** recognition. Hold **10+ years** to **exclude post-investment appreciation**. Track on **Form 8949** and **Form 8997**; the QOF files **Form 8996**.

1) Identify the gain and your **180-day window** (partner gains may start on **K-1 due date**).
2) Invest the gain into a self-certified QOF (partnership/corp).
3) On **Form 8949**, use the QOF code and adjust basis.
4) File **Form 8997** annually to track deferral and holdings.
Yes—invest **only the gain**, not full proceeds, and hit the 180-day deadline. Keep subscription docs, capital calls, and QOF self-certification records with your return.
After **10 years**, elect step-up for QOF interests so the appreciation is **tax-free**. Make the election on sale via **Form 8949/Schedule D** and retain the QOF statements showing holding period.
